perspective:
From Sara Manuelito’s accessible perspective:

- Sara knows she is a speech-language pathologist and that Shirley Whiteplume is a nurse; they are long-time colleagues and close friends at a community health center.
- Sara attended the funeral of a mutual patient. She observed Shirley looking somber and suspected Shirley was deeply affected by the loss.
- Sara told Shirley she knew it was hard and that she had seen how much Shirley cared. She heard Shirley say it had been tough and that she kept thinking something more could have been done. Sara responded that they did everything they could and should remember the good care and joy they brought the patient. Shirley said it was hard to let go.
- During a coffee break at work, Sara brought up their treatment decisions and sensed Shirley felt burdened. Shirley told Sara she felt responsible and wondered if pushing for a different approach might have helped. Sara said they made the best decisions with the information they had and that Shirley should not carry it alone. Shirley said she appreciated that but found it hard to accept.
- In a quiet office moment, Sara observed Shirley being reserved and minimally expressive. Sara told her it was okay to be open. Shirley said she was not sure she could and did not want to seem unprofessional or weak. Sara said showing emotion does not make someone weak. Shirley said maybe Sara was right and she would try to be more open.
- Later, Sara felt her previous confrontation may have been too harsh and apologized. Shirley said it had been a bit much but that she knew Sara meant well and appreciated the apology. Sara said she was there for Shirley however needed. Shirley thanked her and said they should keep talking because it helped.
- After some time, Sara observed improvements in Shirley’s demeanor. Sara asked how she was feeling. Shirley said she felt better thanks to their talks and Sara’s support. Sara offered to spend more time together outside work. Shirley agreed and suggested planning something for the weekend.

Sara has no access to Shirley’s unspoken feelings beyond what Shirley stated or what Sara directly observed.
